Verb ending shortlist

Every lect's regular ending for each theme, tense and person, laid out as person × number. Candidates are ordered by σ (syllables, counted in the source lect's own phonology), then by support. Thin = fewer than 5 verbs back it. 35 lects have regular data.

Terms
σ
Syllable count: the number of vowel peaks the ending (or word) adds. fr -ent 0σ, ro -ați 1σ, es -amos 2σ.
Glide
An i or u said as a consonant, /j/ or /w/ (the y in yes). It never makes a syllable.
Diphthong
A vowel plus a glide in one syllable. Falling: es -áis, -éis, ca -eu. Rising: it -iamo, ro -ea. 1σ.
Hiatus
Two neighbouring vowels in separate syllables: es -ía (co-mí-a), pt comia, it finii. Each counts 1σ.
Inchoative infix
A piece some verbs insert between stem and ending (it fin-isc-o); counted as stem.
Support
The number after a lect: how many regular verbs in that lect-class use the ending.
